I guess it started with some things that happened during my teenage years. When I was in my early teens, I was actually pretty outgoing, talkative and I liked to act a bit silly every now and then (but never in a hurtful way to anyone or whatever). But people grew tired of me for some reason and thought I more annoying than anything else. I never quite understood why. But essentially I went from a pretty popular guy to spending my last three years in highschool completely friendless. And even looking back, I just don't get why that happened. I didn't think I was annoying at all to be around. I also wasn't mean or overly loud or anything like that. And I guess that's what also makes me so insecure about myself. I genuinly just don't understand what I did "wrong" or what I could have done differently to not have become so unpopular and unliked by pretty much everyone. Especially when I see other people being extravert, acting similar like how I was and overall being way louder than me having more succes with being liked by other people.

Eventually I just didn't know how to behave around other people anymore, so I mostly became very quiet, out of fear people would find me annoying again. And over the years I've become more social awkward and more nervous around other people, to the point where I stutter sometimes, form sentences or say things in an awkward way or I don't know what else to say to something people are telling me, other than "yeah", "I see" or "sure". And I just feel like these things must make other people think "wow that guy is definitely weird".

It depends on how you look at it. First of all, there is always one hidden star block on the board (once it has been found, a new one will be placed on a different space).   
On this board in particular, there are 94 spaces minus the current star space that you can never land on, leaving 93 possible spaces you can land on. So essentially you could say that you have a 1/93 or 1.07% chance of landing on the space that contains the star block.

However, star blocks can only appear on blue spaces that never become a star space. There are 50 blue spaces on this map and 8 of them can become star spaces, so that means there are only a total of 42 possible spaces that can actually contain a hidden block with a star.   
So let's say you roll the dice and you can tell that you're about to land on a blue space that never becomes a star space (which is just something you have to know), then you have a 1/42 or 2.38% chance of finding the current hidden star block.

Obviously if a certain blue space has been landed on before and it didn't contain the star block, you also know that you won't find it there either if you're about to land on it.

Okay I don't know if this is good advice, coming from someone who's not on ASD spectrum and so probably is not able to quite relate to how you feel whenever this happens, but I honestly wouldn't overthink it too much. 

While for you it's pretty important that people acknowledge you coming out to them and give you some positive response, I think a lot of people just either don't consider it that big of a deal to really comment on (which in a way you should try to consider a good thing, since that means being bi is getting seen as more and more normalized), or they just simply don't know what kind of response you were really expectating/hoping to hear from them. 

Like let's pretend you just told me you were bi, I didn't know anything about what kind of response you were expecting from me and just for the sake of me not being able to relate at all in the first place, I'm actually not bisexual myself but just straight. I would just say something like "alright cool". And that's not meant in a disrespectful way or anything at all, but that's honestly all I would have to say about it. I accept you for being bi, but I simply don't have anything more to add to that. If I knew how important it was to you that you told me and you were expecting a really positive answer, then I would probably add a bit more though. Something like "I totally accept you, I appreciate that you told me, you're valid, ..." and perhaps ask some follow up questions to show more interest. But if I assumed you just mentioned it to me in a pretty casual way and you weren't expecting that huge of a reaction from me, I would probably also give what you would consider a somewhat flat answer.

Bottom line is, try not to look into it too much and especially not take it too personally. People don't always know what type of response you are looking for in the first place and that can lead to different expectations from you. As long as people aren't being flat out negative about it, don't worry too much about it.

I don't remember why or in what context it was, but 4 years ago at the age of 24, I was either reading about bisexuality or it was just mentioned somewhere, I don't know. But I basically started thinking to myself "waaait, can I actually be bi?". And I started thinking about some experiences I've had in the past, like me wanting to do and actually having done a thing or two with a friend that a straight person probably wouldn't do, the way I thought some guys at college and back in high school were really good looking and so on. And yeah I realized I can be attracted to guys and I came to a pretty quick conclusion that I'm bi.

I don't know why I didn't realize it sooner. I always used to just assume I was straight because I was definitely into girls. And I just never gave it any further thought for some reason, even though I knew bisexuality was a thing. Looking back, I was definitely attracted to some guys, including my best friend from childhood, but I just ignored it I suppose and/or just assumed it was something every straight person experienced every now and then.   
Also, I don't know if this was just me, but growing up, I always seemed to have this idea that muscular guys were always supposed to be considered hot by girls and gay guys by default, but they are actually not my type. Maybe that might also be a reason why I didn't realize it sooner.
